title: Seeing the Riemann Hypothesis Hold: A Live Weil Positivity Gauge for Zeta and Dirichlet L-Functions
gist: VIDRAFT releases a live Hugging Face Space that computes the lowest eigenvalue of Weil's quadratic form (via Suzuki's operator), showing it positive for zeta and four Dirichlet L-functions and negative for single-ingredient imitations, as a visual complement to Levent Alpöge's Claude-assisted 17.4M-line Lean proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. VIDRAFT also independently recompiled that proof and Lean-verified ten lemmas on the operator's constants.

insights.claim: Levent Alpöge announced on 20 November 2026 a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis found with Anthropic's Claude and released as 17.4 million lines of Lean.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: An AI-assisted, machine-checkable proof of a flagship open math problem is a major capability milestone for Anthropic/Claude in formal reasoning; watch for follow-on verification and adoption of AI-for-math tooling.
insights.quote: On 20 November 2026 Levent Alpöge announced a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, found with Claude and released as 17.4 million lines of Lean.

insights.claim: VIDRAFT independently compiled the released Riemann Hypothesis Lean proof from scratch (175,187 files, Lean 4.33.1, Mathlib 0df444a3) and queried the Lean kernel for the axioms of the final theorem, with a 192-core node building the tree at 250 files per minute.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Third-party reproducibility of a 17.4M-line AI-generated proof shows formal verification scales as a trust layer for AI output, but requires substantial compute.
insights.quote: A 192-core node builds the tree at 250 files per minute.

insights.claim: The released proof's Main.lean states the theorems riemannHypothesis, riemannZeta_eq_zero_re, LFunction_ne_zero_of_half_lt_re and LFunction_eq_zero_re, indicating it covers L-function zero statements beyond the zeta function alone.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Scope of the formal statement matters for how big the claimed result is; the generalized L-function statements broaden the milestone.

insights.claim: A formal proof establishes that a statement holds but does not make it visible; VIDRAFT positions a live numerical instrument as a complement that shows the Riemann Hypothesis holding.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: As AI produces enormous unreadable formal proofs, tooling that makes results interpretable to humans becomes a distinct product category.
insights.quote: A formal proof establishes that the statement holds. We release an instrument that shows it holding.

insights.claim: By Weil's 1952 criterion the Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to the positivity of a quadratic form; VIDRAFT's gauge computes the lowest eigenvalue of this form, realized as the self-adjoint operator introduced by Masatoshi Suzuki (arXiv:2606.09096).
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: The instrument rests on a classical equivalence, so a negative eigenvalue for a genuine L-function would be a counterexample signal; positivity is consistent with the proof.
insights.quote: By Weil's criterion the Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to this form never being negative.

insights.claim: Suzuki's paper contains no numerics; VIDRAFT gave the first numerical realization of the operator in July 2026, obtained the closed form of the Archimedean spectrum, and measured the lowest eigenvalue for the zeta function.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Small labs are filling the gap between pure-math theory and computation, building reputational assets on the Hugging Face platform.

insights.claim: The gauge discretizes the form with P1 finite elements with 8x oversampling and uses a Rayleigh-Ritz convergence diagnostic: a ratio λ(N=800)/λ(N=1600) equal to one marks a measured value, while a ratio near four marks a value below numerical resolution, and only measured values are reported as signs.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: The explicit convergence test guards against false-positive sign claims, a reusable standard for evaluating numerical evidence.

insights.claim: The full Weil positivity experiment reproduces in about thirty seconds on a free CPU, with every figure computed live in the visitor's Hugging Face Space session.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Low-cost reproducibility via Hugging Face Spaces shows the platform's role as distribution for research instruments, not just models.
insights.quote: The full experiment reproduces in about thirty seconds on a free CPU.

insights.claim: The Riemann zeta function and four Dirichlet L-functions (conductors 3, 4, 5, 8) give a positive lowest eigenvalue of Weil's form at every resolved interval size.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Numerical consistency with the announced proof adds independent evidence for the result's correctness.

insights.claim: Three imitation objects that each alter a single ingredient of a genuine L-function (removing the pole term, wrong Gamma parity, or flipped prime signs) give negative lowest eigenvalues converged with a mesh ratio of 1.000, showing the quadratic form separates arithmetic objects from look-alikes.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Negative controls make the positivity signal meaningful rather than an artifact of the numerics.
insights.quote: The quadratic form separates arithmetic objects from objects that only resemble them.

insights.claim: The imitation with flipped prime signs coincides with the genuine χ₃ L-function until the first prime enters the interval at a = (log 2)/2, and turns negative immediately after, isolating the prime weights as the cause.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Pinpoints the arithmetic of primes as what drives positivity, a clean mechanistic result.

insights.claim: For Dirichlet L-functions the resolvable window of the gauge extends to a = 1.0, twice the window available for the zeta function, and the zeta row reproduces VIDRAFT's July 2026 measurement to ten digits.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Stable ten-digit reproduction supports the reliability of the instrument.
insights.quote: The zeta row reproduces the July 2026 measurement to ten digits.

insights.claim: The eigenfunctions of the Weil operator vanish at the endpoints as (log(1/d))^(-1/2), the optimal boundary regularity rate of the logarithmic Laplacian, consistent with the operator's principal symbol log|D|.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: A new analytic link between the Weil operator and the logarithmic Laplacian literature; mainly of academic interest.

insights.claim: The Archimedean spectrum of the operator has closed form μ_k = log(k - 1/2) + γ + log(π/2), with the one-half offset identified via the Cyclic Phase Hypothesis of VIDRAFT chairman Taebong Kim as a boundary Maslov phase, confirmed by a Dirichlet-to-Neumann sweep moving the offset from -1/2 to +1/2.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: An in-house hypothesis credited to the company chairman; treat as a lab claim pending outside review.

insights.claim: VIDRAFT verified ten statements on the Archimedean constants of the operator in Lean 4.37.0-rc1 with Mathlib using standard axioms only, including that the spectral constant B₀ = log q - 2 log 2 depends on the conductor alone.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Pairing numerics with Lean-checked lemmas reflects a growing norm of formally verified AI-era mathematics, a tailwind for Lean/Mathlib ecosystems.
insights.quote: Ten statements on the Archimedean constants of the operator are verified by the Lean 4 kernel.
